name: Six Thinking Hats
use_case: A meeting protocol in which everyone deliberately adopts the same mode of thinking at the same time — facts, feelings, caution, optimism, creativity, or process — rather than each person defending a fixed position. Best used when a discussion has polarised into advocates and critics, when the same sceptic is dismissed every time, or when a group needs to explore an idea properly before judging it.
strengths: separates critique from generation so ideas are not killed on arrival
everyone criticises together, so the sceptic is not the designated villain
the feelings mode legitimises intuition that would otherwise stay unsaid
keeps meetings moving because everyone is doing the same thing at once
weaknesses: feels contrived and needs a facilitator willing to hold the frame
the metaphor is easily mocked in cultures that dislike ceremony
produces a rich discussion but no ranking or decision by itself
poor fit for a two-person conversation
